decision.what: JSDoc source: parse fetched/read SOURCE TEXT, not Function.toString()
decision.why: toString() returns only the function's own body, never a comment written above it in the file — there is no way to recover a JSDoc block from it. Reading the defining file's text (fs.readFileSync on Node, fetch() in the browser, both already unbundled and served as-is) is the only route that can see the comment at all.
decision.alternative: toString() — rejected outright, not just less convenient: it cannot work.

log.msg: BUG found and fixed by the browser prototype: the first JSDoc-from-source-text regex (/\*\*([\s\S]*?)\*/\s*method\s*() used a lazy match starting from the TOP of the class body, so a method's failed match (found a DIFFERENT method's doc first) made the lazy quantifier swallow past that comment and grab the NEXT one, splicing two docs together. Silent in proto/objects.mjs because its one six-assertion check only read Agents.list's summary, never Agents.stop's (both are in the same class, stop is #2). Caught the moment proto/browser.html's real View subclass (two @public methods) rendered set_label's summary as list-then-set_label's doc concatenated. Fixed in both files: find the METHOD's own definition line first, then look immediately above it for a directly-adjacent doc comment — never a scan from the top.

decision.what: exposing rule: only a method whose JSDoc carries @public
decision.why: an object like servex.agents mixes framework plumbing (assign, initialize) with genuinely operator-useful methods (list, stop); enumerable-alone would expose all of it, and JSDoc already has to be read for the tool description, so requiring @public on that same comment is an explicit allowlist at no extra cost.
decision.alternative: everything enumerable — rejected: too much accidental surface, and it is a blocklist-shaped decision (exclude the bad ones) instead of an allowlist, which is exactly the shape that made eval dangerous.

log.msg: node proto/objects.mjs: 6/6 PASS (list_objects finds all 4 paths; describe(servex.agents) = [list, stop] only, not assign; each method's summary is its OWN, not its neighbour's; call() runs the real method; call() refuses a non-@public method; resolve() refuses a __proto__ path segment).

assign.outcome:
**Object layer designed and proven on paper** — one `{target, method, args}` envelope for Servex↔dashboard, dev server↔browser and MCP, three generic tools (`list_objects`, `describe`, `call`), and JSDoc read straight from a module's own source text as the tool doc — no build step, no `toString()`.

[The page](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/object-layer/) · [envelope.md](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/object-layer/doc/envelope.md) · [security.md](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/object-layer/doc/security.md) · [build-plan.md](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/object-layer/doc/build-plan.md) · [proto/objects.mjs](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/object-layer/proto/objects.mjs) · [proto/browser.html](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/object-layer/proto/browser.html)

The Node prototype runs 6/6 PASS: `list_objects` finds all four expected paths, `describe("servex.agents")` exposes only its two `@public` methods (never `assign`) with each one's own JSDoc summary, `call` both runs the real method and refuses a non-`@public` one, and `resolve` refuses a `__proto__` path segment. The browser half proved the same `describe` reading JSDoc from a real `View` subclass's own fetched source, headless on a private port, in 9.3ms — screenshot below. Along the way it caught a real bug: the first JSDoc parser spliced two methods' doc comments together the moment a class had more than one, silent in the Node six-assertion set until the browser proof exposed it on a two-method class; fixed in both files before landing. What's left is named as four dispatchable briefs in `build-plan.md` — the real Node root inside Servex, the browser root over `dev/Socket`, a dashboard view built on `describe`, and retiring `eval` in favour of `call`.
